result:
**Rebuttal to Debater B**

Debater B's own example refutes the claim. K₂,ₙ₋₂ is HIST-free with 2n−4 edges, but it is not extremal. At n = 13, my construction (K₁₀ plus the path v₁–a–b–c–v₂) is 2-connected, HIST-free, and has 49 edges, against 22 for K₂,₁₁. A maximum must be at least every valid example, so 2n−4 cannot be the answer.

B asks me to check my graph explicitly, so here it is. In any spanning tree, a, b, and c have G-degree 2, so each must be a leaf. b's neighbours are a and c, so b hangs off one of them, say a. Then a has tree degree at least 2 (b plus the path toward v₁ or v₂), which is forbidden. The symmetric case for c fails the same way. So no HIST exists.

B's "dense graphs are flexible" heuristic doesn't hold here. The dense part is a clique, and the three special vertices are forced into degree-2 positions. B's threshold argument is also speculative; n ≥ 13 is what makes K_{n−3} large enough for the upper-bound arguments, not evidence for a sparse family.

The upper bound is where the scrutiny belongs, but B has offered no graph beating 49 at n = 13.
